newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firmer in U.S. led move.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firmer in U.S. led move.

text.p: May gas oil on the IPE ended Monday firmer on the back of a mainly U.S.-led move, brokers said. Good pre-expiry buying on the prompt NYMEX crude contract helped maintain the firmness seen earlier on the IPE.
May IPE gas oil closed up two dollars a tonne at $165.50, just 25 cents off the day's high.
The May NYMEX crude contract, which expires on Tuesday, saw good short-covering on Monday.
"The most important factor in the market today is short covering on the prompt (NYMEX crude) contract," one broker said.
"There was nothing special happening on gas oil today - it just took the lead from the U.S.," another broker said.
June Brent followed NYMEX crude closely, trading at 1657 GMT up 44 cents at $18.36, off the day's high of $18.48 a barrel.
Brokers said the contract had so far failed to fill the gap between $18.40-50 but might make a further attempt before the close on Monday.
"The funds are coming in to buy but from a technical point of view we need to be a bit cautious because the volumes are not great," one broker said.

Prices were also supported on news that Iraq planned to send helicopters into a no-fly zone in order to pick up returning pilgrims. The White House urged Iraq to reconsider its decision, and that it would 'respond appropriately' but said it would not shoot down civilian helicopters.
